subject: Nebula private deployment — data residency, logging, and egress next steps
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Jared Miller <jared@nebula.fin>, Sanya Patel <sanya.patel@nebula.fin>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-24T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Nebula private deployment — data residency, logging, and egress next steps

Hi Jared / Sanya —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we can align on Nebula's private deployment constraints before we scope the pilot: 

Summary of what we heard:
- Primary requirement: all user PII and transaction payloads must remain within Nebula's us-east-1 VPC and not persist outside of their private deployment.
- Audit/logging: Nebula needs application-level access logs and retention for 3 years; security team wants tamper-evident logs and an option to ship copies to their Splunk instance.
- Egress: outbound network calls from the private runtime may only terminate to approved Nebula endpoints; no public internet egress for model payloads (telemetry & metrics allowed to Redwood observability endpoints if explicitly approved).
- Air-gap option: Nebula asked about an air-gapped on-prem setup for Prod with periodic secure bundle exchanges for model updates.

Proposed next steps (action owners in parentheses):
1) Nebula to share a minimal data map (PII fields + which flows are in-scope). (Jared)
2) Redwood to provide a trimmed data flow diagram for the private runtime showing where temporary KV cache/keys live and exactly what leaves the VPC during warmup/updates. (Naomi + Ben)
3) Security appendix: provide our logging controls (integrity checks, signing, retention options) and a proposed Splunk-forwarder flow. (Marissa)
4) Decide whether a fully air-gapped pilot is required for Beta or if a VPC-only private deployment with strict egress allowlist is sufficient. (Nebula execs + Redwood)

Attachments: I attached a draft data-map template (nebula_data_map_v1.pdf) and our logging matrix (redwood_logging_matrix.xlsx) — please fill the data map and return by EOD Thursday so we can lock the pilot scope for next week's internal sizing.

If you want, we can run a short follow-up (30 min) to confirm the Splunk forwarder details and egress allowlist. Would Thursday 10–10:30 ET work?

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0198

Date: 2027-08-24T12:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Nebula private deployment — data residency, logging, and egress next steps

Naomi —

Appreciate the clear breakdown. A few clarifications from our side after internal sync: 
- Data map: we'll return the filled template by Thursday EOD as requested. Note that our transaction payloads include derived identifiers that must be treated as PII.
- Logs: Splunk forward is required; Nebula security wants logs to be signed and immutable for the first 90 days, then archived with integrity hashes for the remainder of retention.
- Egress: We cannot allow any model telemetry or prompt payloads to be routed off our VPC in Prod. For the pilot, we can accept a VPC-only deployment with allowlisted Redwood endpoints inside our partner VPC peering, provided we can review the exact endpoints.
- Air-gap: Air-gapped on-prem for Prod is a hard requirement if the platform persists model artifacts or KV caches outside Nebula control. For the pilot, we prefer VPC-only unless Redwood confirms no persistent external artifacts.

Let's take the Thursday slot — 10:00 ET works. Will loop in our infra lead if any of the API/network folks need to join.

Regards,
Jared Miller
Head of Platform Security | Nebula Financial
jared@nebula.fin
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Jared Miller <jared@nebula.fin>, Sanya Patel <sanya.patel@nebula.fin>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-25T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Nebula private deployment — data residency, logging, and egress next steps

Jared / Sanya —

Thanks — some quick technical points to set expectations ahead of Thursday: 
- Model artifacts & KV cache: Redwood's private runtime keeps model artifacts on the customer's provisioned storage (mounted volumes inside the VPC) by default. KV cache is memory-resident on the inference nodes and not persisted to our control plane. We will include a diagram to show volumes + node boundaries.
- Telemetry: by default we emit anonymized runtime metrics to Redwood's observability; we can suppress those in Nebula's deployment and only enable them if you opt-in.
- Splunk forwarding: we support two options — push-forward from the runtime to your Splunk HEC inside the VPC, or an S3-delivery + Nebula ingestion workflow. Both support signing/immutability controls (we can sign logs with a rotating key pair and provide integrity hashes).
- Egress allowlist: we'll provide a short list of endpoints that need to be allowed for update-bundles and image pulls (if allowed). For an air-gapped setup, those will be replaced with a signed bundle transfer process.

I'll attach a quick egress diagram and the draft sign/forward flow before the call — see private-vpc-egress-diagram.png in the thread. Naomi / Marissa: can you add the Splunk forwarding options to the appendix?

Ben Carter
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

Legal will want a short appendix that spells out the retention guarantees and the exact signing/hash algorithm we use for tamper evidence (we typically propose SHA-256 with HMAC around delivery bundles). Also include a short SLA excerpt around support response times in the event of ingestion failures.

Jared — we can include the appendix in the pilot SOW. Naomi — can you draft the appendix and share a first pass by Friday morning so I can run it by Legal?
